newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen AG in talks with transport suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen AG in talks with transport suppliers.

text.p: Thyssen AG has held co-operation talks with transport suppliers but has no current plans for any acquisitions or joint ventures in the logistics field, company chairman Dr Dieter Volga said.

Vogel told Reuters at Germany freight manager congress here that the Germany conglomerate planned in particular to expand in East Asia but would do this alone through subsidiary Thyssen Haniel Logistic GmbH (THI).
We have had negotiations in the past but we have no plans at present for any co-operations," he said at the annual German Logistics Congress in Berlin.
Vogel declined to say whether THI had spoken with any of the transport integrators, in light of recent alliance between TNT and Schenker International, and UPS and Danzas.
Vogel said subsidiary Thyssen Haniel Logistic had had losses in U.S. operations over a five-year period but had now recovered again.
Parent company Thyssen AG would have a growing need for air and sea transport logistics as part of its globalisation driver in the coming years, Vogel noted.
Thyssen AG had a competitive advantage with its own logistics subsidiary, which generated 16 percent of total turnover with the parent company, he said.

Thyssen Haniel Logistics has an annual turnover of 3.2 billion marks and was present in 300 locations in 30 countries offering land, air and sea transport service, he added. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
